page.title: Install SoundTap
lang.label: Language
hero.title: Install SoundTap
hero.intro: Six short steps take your Bose SoundTouch from Bose's software to SoundTap. The install itself takes about five minutes.
alpha.text: SoundTap is alpha software. It replaces everything on the speaker, including the part that starts it. There is a way back to Bose (step 6): read it before you start.
s1.title: Which speaker do you have?
s1.otherHelp: Have another model? Help bring it up: the first step is read-only investigation.
s2.title: What you need
need.speaker: The speaker plugged in and still running Bose's software.
need.versionAny: Recent Bose software. Pick your speaker above to see which version it needs.
need.version: Bose software {minimum} or newer on the {model}. Older software: update Bose first, in the Bose app.
need.versionWhere: The Bose app shows the version under Settings, Speaker settings, your speaker, About.
need.computer: For the easiest route: a computer (Mac, Windows or Linux) on the same Wi-Fi as the speaker, and a speaker that can reach the internet.
need.phone: Without internet: a phone or computer with a web browser.
need.boseFile: For the way back: Bose's own update file for your model (Update.stu), saved before you start. SoundTap does not ship it. Why and how
s3.title: Install automatically
s3.what: One line on your computer finds the SoundTouch speakers on your network that still run Bose's software and asks which ones get SoundTap. Each speaker you pick downloads SoundTap itself and installs it.
s3.safe: Nothing is installed on your computer, and only the speakers you pick are changed. Curious? Read install.sh or install.ps1.
s3.mobile: This looks like a phone or tablet. The automatic installer runs on a computer; from a phone, use step 4.
os.label: Your computer
os.mac.1: Open Terminal: press ⌘ + Space, type Terminal and press Enter.
os.mac.2: Copy the line below, paste it into Terminal and press Enter.
os.windows.1: Open PowerShell: click Start, type PowerShell and press Enter.
os.windows.2: Copy the line below, paste it into PowerShell (right-click pastes) and press Enter.
os.linux.2: Copy the line below, paste it and press Enter.
os.3: A list of your speakers appears. Answer its questions: each speaker you pick then installs SoundTap, and its setup page opens when it is done.
br.summary: No terminal? Install from this page by IP address (Chrome or Edge)
br.intro: This page asks a SoundTouch that still runs Bose's software to download SoundTap from SoundTap's update feed and install it. The speaker stays on your Wi-Fi and does the work itself; it restarts as SoundTap after about four minutes.
br.browsers: Chrome and Edge ask you once to let this page reach devices on your local network: allow it. Firefox and Safari cannot reach a speaker from this page; use step 4 instead.
br.versionPlaceholder: As the Bose app shows it
br.versionHint: In the Bose app: Settings, Speaker settings, your speaker, About.
br.ipHint: In the Bose app: Settings, Speaker settings, your speaker, About. Or look it up in your router.
br.agree: I understand that SoundTap is alpha software that replaces everything on the speaker, and I have read how to go back to Bose (step 6).
br.pickModel: Pick your speaker in step 1 first.
br.trust: The page cannot read the model or its software from the speaker, so it takes your word for both.
br.tableFailed: The list of supported speakers could not be loaded. Reload the page.
judge.noModel: {model}: not supported yet. SoundTap has not run on it, so this page will not install it.
judge.no: Not supported yet. SoundTap has not run on this model, so this page will not install it.
judge.unread: Type the Bose software version the Bose app shows for this speaker.
judge.old: Bose software {version}: the {model} needs {minimum} or later. Update Bose first, in the Bose app.
st.askingDetail: If your browser asks to access devices on your local network, allow it.
st.noAnswer: No answer from a SoundTouch with Bose's software at {host}.
st.noAnswerDetail: Check the address, and allow local network access if the browser asked. Firefox and Safari cannot do this from a web page: use Chrome or Edge, or step 4.
st.uncertain: The request could not be confirmed.
st.uncertainDetail: The speaker may have received it. Keep it powered while this page checks for SoundTap.
st.sentDetail: Leave the speaker alone and keep it powered.
st.stockAnswers: The stock service still answers. The install has not been confirmed. Keep the speaker powered.
st.restarting: The speaker may be restarting or unreachable. Keep it powered; waiting for its SoundTap version.
st.open: Open SoundTap to set it up.
st.notStarted: The install did not start or has not finished.
st.notStartedDetail: The stock service still answers after {minutes} minutes. The request may have been refused or the update feed unreachable. Check the speaker before retrying; see step 4.
st.unconfirmedDetail: Keep the speaker powered. Open http://{host}/ to check it. The browser may be blocking the version check, or the speaker may still be restarting.
s4.title: Without internet: upload the file
s4.intro: Use this when the speaker has no internet, or when step 3 did not work. A phone with a browser is enough.
s4.step1: Download the SoundTap file. The same file works on every model.
dl.sha256Only: Its checksum is in the .sha256 file next to it.
dl.none: No SoundTap Core release has been published yet. Test builds for testers are on the releases page.
dl.error: The latest release could not be looked up. Download SoundTap-Core-X.Y.Z.stu from the latest release.
dl.checkText: Compare the checksum above with the one your computer prints for the file:
s4.step2: Put the speaker in setup mode.
setup.st1020: Hold Preset 2 and Volume − together until the speaker opens its setup network.
setup.manual: Start setup mode as Bose's manual for your speaker describes.
setup.any: SoundTouch 10 or 20: hold Preset 2 and Volume − together until the speaker opens its setup network. Other models: start setup mode as Bose's manual describes.
s4.step3: Join the speaker's Wi-Fi network, named Bose …, with the phone or computer that has the file.
s4.step4: Open the speaker's upload page in the browser:
s4.gateway: The speaker is that network's router, normally at 192.0.2.1; a SoundTouch 20 has used 192.168.1.1. If the page does not open, use the router address your phone or computer shows.
s4.step5: Choose the .stu file and send it. The upload takes two to three minutes: keep the page open until it answers.
s4.onWifi: Is the speaker already on your Wi-Fi with Bose's software? Then setup mode is not needed: open the same page on the speaker's own IP address, for example http://192.168.1.23:17008/update.html.
s4.http500: A first upload has sometimes answered with an error (HTTP 500). Do not send the file again while the speaker may still be writing; the install guide says what to do, and has a route over USB.
s5.title: What happens next
next.wait: Leave the speaker alone and keep it powered. It writes SoundTap, restarts and comes up as SoundTap in about four to six minutes.
next.noPower: Do not pull the power while it is busy, and do not send the file again.
next.st20: A SoundTouch 20 shows the SoundTap splash on its display about a second after it restarts. It then updates its network chip and restarts once more, so allow extra time.
next.st10: A SoundTouch 10 sweeps its lights from side to side while it starts.
next.wifi: Afterwards the speaker joins the Wi-Fi Bose's software was on. If it does not, it opens its own setup network, named after the speaker (for example SoundTap ST10 A1B2C3): join it, and the setup page lets you pick your Wi-Fi. A SoundTouch 20 needs a 2.4 GHz WPA2 network.
next.open: Then open http://soundtap.local on any phone, tablet or computer on the same network. Updates later come from the speaker's own page.
next.stuck: Not back after ten minutes? Keep it powered and see When something goes wrong.
s6.title: The way back to Bose
back.how: On the speaker's own page, open Settings → Updates, choose Bose's Update.stu (the file you saved) and confirm. Hold a button on the speaker for two seconds when it asks, and leave it powered while it writes and restarts.
back.notReset: It is not a factory reset: Bose's software goes back, but not every byte SoundTap wrote is removed.
back.st20: On a SoundTouch 20 the network chip keeps SoundTap's software; putting Bose's back there is still a developer step.
back.rescue: If SoundTap no longer starts, a USB stick puts SoundTap back. The install guide has the details and every exception.
back.help: Stuck? Open an install or recovery issue: we would much rather help than have a speaker end up in a drawer.
foot.guide: The full installation guide has every step in more detail, a USB route and troubleshooting.
foot.source: SoundTap is open source: view it on GitHub. Not affiliated with Bose Corporation.
